lead.title: Show Apple Music stations under Radio
lead.summary: What does this implement/fix? Apple Music stations showed up as dynamic playlists, so users had to look for them under Playlists instead of Radio.
lead.author: MarvinSchenkel

highlights.title: [pca9554] Add a device option with the PCA953x/PCA955x/TCA955x names and the PCAL9538 and PCAL9555 expanders
highlights.summary: What does this implement/fix? Adds a device: option to pca9554 that names the expander model, covers the PCA9534/A, PCA9536, PCA9538, PCA9554/A, PCA9535, PCA9555 and TCA9554/9535/9555 with…
highlights.unlocks: Unlocks: [pca9554] Add a device option with the PCA953x/PCA955x/TCA955x names and the PCAL9538 and PCAL9555 expanders.
highlights.author: ilikecake

highlights.title: [speaker][speaker_source] Add a set volume for announcements that start while nothing is playing
highlights.summary: What does this implement/fix? Today an announcement (TTS, doorbell, timer) always plays at the media player volume.
highlights.unlocks: Unlocks: [speaker][speaker_source] Add a set volume for announcements that start while nothing is playing.
highlights.author: remcom

highlights.title: [mqtt] Add MQTT over WebSocket transport for ESP32 IDF
highlights.summary: What does this implement/fix? Adds a transport option to mqtt so an ESP32 running ESP IDF can reach the broker over a WebSocket ( ws ) or a WebSocket with TLS ( wss ), for brokers behind a…
highlights.unlocks: Unlocks: [mqtt] Add MQTT over WebSocket transport for ESP32 IDF.
highlights.author: ankur-paan

highlights.title: [vl53l1x] Add VL53L1X time-of-flight distance sensor
highlights.summary: What does this implement/fix? Adds a vl53l1x sensor platform for ST's VL53L1X time of flight distance sensor, following the register sequence of ST's Ultra Lite Driver (ULD), with up to 4 m…
highlights.unlocks: Unlocks: [vl53l1x] Add VL53L1X time-of-flight distance sensor.
highlights.author: will-tm

briefs.title: Show the in library icon on artist and album pages
briefs.summary: What does this implement/fix? The new artist and album pages lost the "In library" icon that the other detail pages show.
briefs.author: OzGav

briefs.title: [ci] Add the speaker media player, web_server_idf and MQTT WebSocket flows to the hardware-test skill
briefs.summary: What does this implement/fix? Adds three proven flows to the hardware test skill so the next agent can run them without rediscovering the traps: the speaker media player's pipeline tasks,…
briefs.unlocks: Unlocks: [ci] Add the speaker media player, web_server_idf and MQTT WebSocket flows to the hardware-test skill.
briefs.author: bdraco

briefs.title: zgp: add the Green Power manager, device, and proxy runtime
briefs.summary: Adds the Green Power (GP / GPEP) runtime on top of the types/frame/crypto parsing core: the GreenPowerManager (commissioning, pairing, packet dispatch), the GPDevice model, the proxy table,…
briefs.unlocks: Unlocks: Zgp: add the Green Power manager, device, and proxy runtime.
briefs.author: nmingam

briefs.title: [gree] Add sleep preset support for GREE YAC1FB9
briefs.summary: What does this implement/fix? Adds the sleep preset to the GREE yac1fb9 model, which already had the bit on the wire but no way to set it.
briefs.unlocks: Unlocks: [gree] Add sleep preset support for GREE YAC1FB9.
briefs.author: jrvd007

briefs.title: [core] Share one log_entity_header() for entity dump_config headers
briefs.summary: What does this implement/fix? The entity dump config macros and helpers share one core log entity header() for their ' ' line instead of each carrying its own null check, log call and (on…
briefs.author: bdraco

briefs.title: AudioMuse-AI provider
briefs.summary: What does this implement/fix? Adds an AudioMuse AI plugin provider.
briefs.author: NeptuneHub

briefs.title: [ld2420][ld2450] Use Apply numbers for hub forwarding numbers
briefs.summary: What does this implement/fix? Replace the ld2420 and ld2450 number classes that only store a value or call the hub with the shared number.ApplyNumber , saving 96 to 272 bytes of RAM per build.
briefs.author: bdraco

briefs.title: Add a command to move a track within a playlist
briefs.summary: What does this implement/fix? Lets you move a track within a playlist, as agreed in discussion 4971.
briefs.unlocks: Unlocks: Add a command to move a track within a playlist.
briefs.author: pcc0x

briefs.title: Give collection pages the detail page hero
briefs.summary: What does this implement/fix? Collection pages get the same hero as the other detail pages, instead of the old InfoHeader .
briefs.author: fmunkes

briefs.title: Similar tracks from a similarity plugin take precedence over the music provider
briefs.summary: What does this implement/fix? A similarity plugin such as Sonic Similarity is installed to improve on the similar tracks a streaming service returns, but it was only asked when the track's own music provider had nothing.
briefs.author: MarvinSchenkel

briefs.title: [components] Set optional plain values with cg.add_optional (n-z)
briefs.summary: What does this implement/fix? Moves optional setters in components n to z to cg.add optional (#21180), so each optional key is one line instead of an if block.
briefs.author: bdraco

briefs.title: Fix Sendspin display Play routing to static groups
briefs.summary: What does this implement/fix? When a 'Display' device (with the Controller sendspin role) is in a static group with a Player, it can skip forwards, back, and pause but it is not able to…
briefs.unlocks: Improves reliability around fix Sendspin display Play routing to static groups.
briefs.author: teancom

briefs.title: [tests] Use the exact entity lookups in the integration tests
briefs.summary: What does this implement/fix? This moves the integration tests that filter entities by hand onto the require entity and require only entity helpers, so each lookup is one line and fails with the same clear message.
briefs.unlocks: Unlocks: [tests] Use the exact entity lookups in the integration tests.
briefs.author: bdraco

briefs.title: [components] Set optional plain values with cg.add_optional (a-m)
briefs.summary: What does this implement/fix? Moves optional setters in components a to m to cg.add optional (#21180), so each optional key is one line instead of an if block.
briefs.author: bdraco

briefs.title: feat(camera): server-side session handling for camera API clients
briefs.summary: The Home Assistant camera integration (home assistant/core#176080) is the first external client of the schema 14 camera API.
briefs.author: Apollon77

briefs.title: [epaper_spi] Only compile the driver sources the configured models need
briefs.summary: What does this implement/fix? epaper spi compiled all 18 of its driver .cpp files for every config, whichever model was selected.
briefs.author: jesserockz

briefs.title: [tests] Use require_service in the integration tests
briefs.summary: What does this implement/fix? This moves the integration tests onto require service() from #21150, so each test finds a user service in one line instead of a hand written search followed by an existence check.
briefs.unlocks: Unlocks: [tests] Use require_service in the integration tests.
briefs.author: bdraco

briefs.title: Fix option bullets and stale options the schema generator reports
briefs.summary: The schema generator ( script/schema doc.mjs , #7750) now runs on every esphome schema build and reports what it cannot attach to the language schema.

releasePreviews.title: ESPHome 2026.10.0: Native ESP8266 builds and compressed updates
releasePreviews.body:
ESPHome 2026.10.0: Native ESP8266 builds and compressed updates

Oct 21, 2026
Jesse Hills
ESPHome Developer

NOTE

This is a beta release. Details on this page may change before the stable release is published.

Every month ESPHome ships a release like this one, so you can learn about new features, fixes, and other changes worth knowing about before you update.

Short on time? Here’s the quick version
Section titled “Short on time? Here’s the quick version”

Here’s the plain-language rundown for anyone short on time or newer to ESPHome; the full technical post continues below for anyone who wants it.

Action needed if you use any of these:

Lights with an initial_state: now actually respect it at boot, so if you had a light configured to come up on but it was quietly staying off, double-check the behavior is what you want after updating.

The codec_support_enabled option on speaker media players is gone; remove it from your config and set the pipeline format: to NONE to keep the old behavior, otherwise the config will no longer validate.

IR climate devices with supports_heat: false or supports_cool: false no longer offer the combined heat/cool auto mode by default - add supports_heat_cool: true to bring it back if you were relying on it.

New features: Updates install about a third smaller and proportionally faster on every platform ESPHome supports, and ESP8266 builds are considerably quicker end-to-end, including on recent Apple Silicon Macs that no longer need Rosetta.

Also in this release: 20 new components (including Wi-Fi motion sensing, a persistent counter, a new CO2 sensor, USB-UART bridging and TCP-UART), broader Zigbee cluster coverage, live light transition reporting, CSS color names in light actions, and a long list of smaller fixes and improvements.

If you’re running a typical config, there’s nothing else you need to look at before updating - aside from the items above, your setup should carry over cleanly.

If you’re running custom lambdas, external components, or a non-standard config, or you just want the full technical detail, keep reading below for the full release overview and feature writeups.

Components added in this release

Release overview
Section titled “Release overview”

ESPHome 2026.10.0 lands two platform-wide defaults that touch most of the fleet: the native ESP8266
Arduino toolchain is now the default build path, retiring Rosetta on Apple Silicon and cutting cold
compile time nearly in half, and OTA uploads are compressed on ESP32, RP2040, LibreTiny and host
through a new deflate decoder, so updates ship about a third fewer bytes and finish proportionally
faster on slow or lossy links. The native API’s protobuf and controller-dispatch hot paths got
another round of per-byte and per-instruction optimizations, 20+ field-packing PRs and a sweep
moving codegen data from heap and RAM into flash tables trim RAM across every build, and the
register_apply_action and sub_* codegen helpers remove hundreds of boilerplate C++ classes and
Python lines across more than 150 components with no YAML changes. ESP-IDF builds now run cmake
and ninja directly instead of through idf.py, and a --skip-bootloader flag plus mbedTLS and
tool-startup trims save several more seconds per compile on Home Assistant Green class hardware. On
top of that, 20 new components land, including Wi-Fi CSI motion sensing, USB-UART bridges with mux
and tap seams, TCP-UART and UART-TCP, SPI Ethernet on KSZ8851SNL, a persistent counter sensor and
a Sensirion STCC4 CO2 sensor, alongside a device-side Home Assistant onboarding wizard, outgoing
API connections for NAT-ed devices, broader Zigbee cluster coverage and new light transition,
color, resume-effect and e-paper features. The bundled Device Builder can now flash every supported
chip family from the browser.

Upgrade checklist
Section titled “Upgrade checklist”

If you have ESP8266 devices, expect the first compile to be a clean build on the new native arduino toolchain;
set toolchain: platformio under esp8266: to keep the old path (and plan to migrate before 2027.4.0).

If you set restore_mode: on a light with initial_state: {state: on/off}, verify the boot state is what you
want - lights that previously booted off against your initial_state will now follow it.

If you set codec_support_enabled: on a speaker media player, remove it and switch the pipeline format: to
NONE for the old all behaviour; configs that still carry the key now fail validation.

If you rely on a speaker or speaker_source media player muting itself at volume zero (or firing on_mute /
on_unmute from a volume change), update your automations - volume and mute are now independent.

If you use climate_ir platforms with supports_heat: false or supports_cool: false and want to keep the
heat_cool auto mode, add supports_heat_cool: true.

If you set buffer_size: on remote_receiver for ESP8266, RP2040, LibreTiny, ESP32-C2 or ESP32-C61, multiply the
value by 4 to keep the same number of buffered pulses.

If you have usb_uart entries that could match the same USB device (overlapping VID/PID), split them with
manufacturer and product filters - overlapping entries are now rejected at validation.

If you use epaper_spi with saturated pure green or magenta drawn by RGB value, review the output; monochrome
conversion now uses perceived luminance. Also drop full_update_every above 1 on panels without partial refresh
and add psram: for seeed-reterminal-sticky.

If you have a sendspin switch, add type: enabled to each entry.

If you build for the host platform, remove unsupported platformio_options keys and rewrite any
separate-argument build_flags (such as -include pre.h ) as a single entry; Windows host builds are no longer
supported.

If you use homeassistant.action with more than 255 data/variable keys per action, split it - the config is now
rejected at validation.

If you write lambdas that read tag after a delay in on_tag / on_tag_removed, note that tag is now
passed by reference; existing read-only uses continue to work, but code that modified a local copy of the tag now
modifies the shared reference.

ESP8266 native toolchain by default
Section titled “ESP8266 native toolchain by default”

The native Arduino toolchain foundation that landed dormant in 2026.9.0 is now the default for every
ESP8266 build. @bdraco finished the stack with the compile driver and
dispatch layer ( #18539 ), ESPHome-built xtensa gcc
10.3 archives for Linux x86_64/arm64, macOS x86_64/arm64 and Windows x86_64 served from
esphome-libs/xtensa-lx106-elf-toolchain
instead of the registry package ( #19849 ), and
flipped the default to toolchain: arduino in
#19886. The CI matrix now compiles every ESP8266
component test the same way ( #19714,
#19740 ).

Faster builds end-to-end - on an M5 Max against the same config an esphome compile runs in
9.2s cold instead of 17.8s, a warm-ccache rebuild in 2.8s instead of 7.6s, a no-op rebuild in 0.4s
instead of 2.2s, and a one-line edit in 9.6s instead of 20.7s.

Apple Silicon without Rosetta - the registry package had no arm64 macOS build, so ESP8266
builds on recent Macs needed Rosetta 2, which Apple ends with macOS 28. The ESPHome-built archives
are native on every supported host.

ESP8266 progress in Device Builder - the native build runs through ninja, so its [N/M]
progress counters feed the device builder a compile percentage the way ESP-IDF builds already do.

Opt-out available, deprecated - a custom framework source, a framework version other than
3.1.2, an unlisted board or an unsupported host still work with toolchain: platformio. The
PlatformIO path warns on validation and goes away in 2027.4.0.

Roughly 40% of ESPHome devices run on ESP8266, so the change touches a large slice of the fleet;
the first build after upgrading is a clean build because the build directory’s toolchain changed.

Compressed OTA uploads on ESP32, RP2040, LibreTiny and host
Section titled “Compressed OTA uploads on ESP32, RP2040, LibreTiny and host”

@bdraco extended compressed OTA, which the ESP8266 already had via its
gzip-aware bootloader, to every other platform ESPHome supports
( #19037 ). RP2040 takes the same gzip path through
the Arduino Pico stub. ESP32, LibreTiny and host inflate a raw deflate stream through a 4 KB window
as it arrives, so an image goes over the network about one third smaller than before.

Automatic negotiation - a client bit and a server bit opt in; old clients and old firmware
never see it, so pre-2026.10.0 devices update exactly as before.

Covered by the digest - the client sends the inflated image’s MD5, so the integrity check
covers the decoder.

Big win on slow or lossy links - ESP32-C6 OpenThread, encrypted WiFi with 15% packet loss and
any mesh-hop or VPN upload is transfer-bound; measured on an ESP32 at 15% simulated loss, upload
time drops from 317/113s to 74/67s.

Allocation-safe - the 4.9 KB decoder session is allocated through RAMAllocator::make_unique
so a heap-exhausted device falls back to an uncompressed upload instead of rebooting.

The flash cost is about 2 KB on ESP32 and under 100 bytes on ESP8266 and RP2040 for the negotiation
glue.

API protobuf throughput and controller dispatch
Section titled “API protobuf throughput and controller dispatch”

A sustained push on the native API’s hot paths continued through this release.
@bdraco collapsed the three protobuf decode virtuals into one and
removed the vtable from decode ( #19016,
#19029 ), made generated encode and size entry
points type-erased ( #19015 ), passed the encode
cursor by value through the protobuf helpers so it stays in a register
( #19014 ), counted packed varints a machine word at
a time ( #20122 ), decoded base64 in a single pass
( #20123 ), and kept the write cursor in a register
while emitting sub-message tags inline ( #20124 ).

A separate change dispatches controller updates through generated direct calls instead of a runtime
registry: APIServer and WebServer drop the Controller base class and the state-publish path
goes from 25 instructions with 8 loads and 2 indirect calls to 10 instructions with 2 loads and
direct calls only, costing 256 B less flash and 24 B less RAM on a typical ESP32 build
( #19588 ). The web server also builds state
documents in a stack arena and sends events straight from the caller’s buffers so a state event
does no heap allocation at all ( #19376,
#19383 ).

External components that subclass Controller or hand-write a non-const AudioFile * need small
updates; the migration notes are in each PR.

Memory optimizations across every build
Section titled “Memory optimizations across every build”

@bdraco led a tree-wide sweep to shrink per-instance structures and
move constant codegen data out of RAM.

Field packing - roughly twenty PRs grouped single-byte flags next to other byte fields on
speaker, mixer, i2s_audio, voice_assistant, microphone, sendspin, template, ledc, rtttl, ld2450,
remote_receiver, esp32_ble, improv_ble, wifi and more
( #20135 through
#20152 ), reclaiming three bytes of padding at a
time across many instances.

Empty-base packing - [[no_unique_address]] lets the empty Scheduler mutex, empty script
argument tuple, empty template unused members and the empty WiFi pending_ flags struct take no
space on single-threaded platforms ( #20139,
#20140,
#20141,
#20142 ); App drops from 156 to 152 bytes on
ESP8266.

Light state 12 bytes smaller - the effect index became a uint16_t sharing a word with the
flags, the gamma factor rode along in the flash lookup table, and the flash transition length
only compiles in when a light sets flash_transition_length
( #19711 ). LightState goes from 180 to 168
bytes.

StaticVector and FreeRTOS handles embedded in place - the ring buffer, FreeRTOS queue, static
task and ESP32 logger buffer now use the static structure as their own handle instead of
allocating one next to it ( #20129,
#20133,
#20134 ).

Codegen data in flash - audio files, display init sequences, select options, font glyphs, RC
switch protocols, allowed origins, UDP addresses, BLE MAC filter lists, matrix keypad keys, Home
Assistant action fields and select.is option lists are now constexpr tables in flash instead of
heap or RAM objects built in setup() ( #20072,
#20079,
#20081,
#20085,
#20086,
#20088,
#20089,
#20090,
#20091,
#20108,
#20110,
#20117,
#20237 ); the Voice PE config saves 192 B of RAM
and 272 B of flash from the audio files change alone.

Header inlining - trivial single-store setters moved into headers on template, bme280_base,
bme680, bmp280_base, mqtt_subscribe, tsl2561, tsl2591, esp32_camera, web_server, waveshare_epaper,
bang_bang, graphical_display_menu, adc, thermostat, openthread, st7789v, max44009, sds011, haier,
lc709203f ( #19278 through
#19299 ) and setters that pass defaults are
skipped at codegen on api, template, uart and version
( #19227,
#19232,
#20066,
#20067,
#20069 ).

ESP8266 log tags and flash strings - every ESPHOME_LOG_TAG on ESP8266 now rides in flash
( #20290,
#19574,
#19578 ) and the long-inert
esp8266_store_log_strings_in_flash option that forced them into RAM is deprecated and ignored
( #19577 ).

ESP32 unused subsystems trimmed - a flash_chip option under esp32: framework: advanced:
drops the unused flash-vendor driver tables, saving up to 5 KB of RAM and image on an ESP32-S3
with octal flash ( #19217 ), and
nvs_cache_in_psram moves ESP-IDF’s internal NVS page cache into PSRAM for an extra ~10 KB of
internal heap on boards with guaranteed PSRAM
( #19378 ).

Codegen architecture: register_apply_action
Section titled “Codegen architecture: register_apply_action”

@bdraco finished one of the largest coordinated refactors in recent
memory. register_apply_action and register_apply_condition turn an action or condition that
only forwards config values to its parent into a field table with no C++ class and no builder, with
constants and inline lambdas baked into one stateless function
( #19469,
#19655 ).

Over 80 components moved onto it in this release, covering actions and conditions on cover, fan,
climate, light, switch, valve, lock, number, text, select, event, media_player, speaker,
voice_assistant, mqtt, globals, update, ledc, esp32_ble_tracker, alarm_control_panel, rtttl,
sprinkler, servo, haier, midea, mitsubishi_cn105, nextion, dfplayer, hlk_fm22x, max7219digit,
fingerprint_grow, ezo_pmp, sim800l, senseair, scd30, scd4x, sen5x, nau7802, ds1307, pcf8563,
pcf85063, rx8130, bm8563, pzemac, pzemdc, bl0906, cm1106, hc8, htu21d, hdc302x, cs5460a, cc1101,
sx126x, sx127x, pulse_counter, pulse_meter, display_menu_base, hub75, snapshot, router, animation,
rotary_encoder, audio_dac, online_image, duty_time, pipsolar, aic3204, pmwcs3, mcp4461, ufire_ec,
ufire_ise, max6956, grove_tb6612fng, hbridge, lightwaverf, openthread, mixer, speaker_source,
emontx, zigbee and more. The parallel register_apply_condition sweep covered switch, binary
sensor, fan, light, media player, script, lock, time, mqtt, speaker, display, pn532, tinyusb,
voice_assistant, sun, alarm_control_panel and pid.

Each converted action is one pointer per action instead of one per field, with no per-component
action class. Alongside it a shared register_simple_action / register_parented_action /
register_bare_condition set covers the three remaining builder shapes
( #19321,
#19322 ). The removed action classes were only
instantiated by codegen and never reachable from user lambdas, so no YAML changes.

Sub-entity codegen helpers
Section titled “Sub-entity codegen helpers”

Over 150 hub components wired up optional child entities with the same three-line pattern per key.
@bdraco added new_sub_sensor, new_sub_binary_sensor and
new_sub_text_sensor on top of a shared entity_helpers module, then expanded to seven entity
types with bound sub_* helpers ( #19725,
#19754 ). Over 100 components moved to the new
helpers across this release’s merge window, covering ina2xx_base, pzemac/pzemdc, bl0906/bl0939/
bl0940/bl0942, hlw8012/hlw8032, cse7766, scd30, bme280_base, bme680, bmp280_base/bmp3xx_base/
bmp581_base/spa06_base/mlx90393, bmp085/dps310/lps22/mpl3115a2/ms5611, hdc1080/hdc2010/hdc2080/
hdc302x/hte501, aht10/am2315c/am2320/dht/dht12, atm90e26/atm90e32, ld2410/ld2412/ld2420/ld2450,
sgp30, sgp4x, pmsx003, sps30, hm3301, sun_gtil2, veml7700, tsl2591, tcs34725, hmc5883l, htu21d,
ccs811, inkbird_ibsth1_mini, mopeka_pro_check / mopeka_std_check, kuntze, ufm01, alpha3, max9611,
ufire_ec/ufire_ise, kmeteriso, mcp9600, airthings_wave_base/airthings_wave_plus, ruuvitag,
seeed_mr24hpc1/seeed_mr60bha2/seeed_mr60fda2, mhz19, growatt_solar, havells_solar, sdm_meter,
wireguard, pm2005, ee895, mmc5603/mmc5983, gdk101, smt100, pmwcs3, emc2101, ens160_base, zyaura,
cs5460a, es8388, sht3xd, shtcx, combination, libretiny, sound_level, bthome_mithermometer,
atc_mithermometer, pvvx_mithermometer and a dozen Xiaomi BLE sensors.

Each converted hub drops from three lines per key to a single sub_sensor(), sub_binary_sensor()
or sub_text_sensor() call, so a 600-line hub config in Python becomes a few dozen declarative
calls while the generated main.cpp stays identical.

ESP-IDF build speed
Section titled “ESP-IDF build speed”

@bdraco replaced the idf.py wrapper with direct cmake and ninja
calls, matching the native ESP8266 and host paths
( #19871 ). The firmware is byte-identical across
nine scenarios on ESP-IDF 5.5.5 and 6.1.0 and a CI check runs the real idf.py on a freshly built
tree so an IDF bump cannot drift unnoticed. The win is Python startup and the removed second
ninja all: about 5 seconds saved per build on a Home Assistant Green.

Several supporting pieces compound the saving.

--skip-bootloader flag for OTA-only builds disables the bootloader sub-build when the
update will never deliver one, saving 7.5 s per compile on a warm ccache on an M5 Max and
proportionally more on Green-class hardware ( #19925 ).

Build-and-size in one ninja run instead of two
( #19997 ) and the json2 size data emitted so
the link edge is not blocked ( #18848 ).

ESP-IDF tool paths resolved once per build and the IDF version read in-process instead of
starting idf_tools ( #19996,
#19998 ).

mbedTLS trimmed to the client-only defaults needed by ESPHome’s HTTPS and MQTT paths, and
disabled entirely when no component needs crypto
( #18877,
#19088 ).

nRF52 shared ccache between devices and native-toolchain cache settings
( #20027,
#20028 ).

Native API outgoing connections
Section titled “Native API outgoing connections”

@bdraco added outgoing_connection under api: so the device opens
the native API connection itself instead of waiting to be reached
( #18919 ). With no host: the device remembers the
last dial-back client and reconnects when that client stops reaching it; with host: set the
device always dials out, which covers a peer behind NAT or on a routed segment it cannot reach
inbound.

Noise only - the option requires encryption: because the connection can leave the LAN and
the shared key is the only trustworthy way to verify the peer.

Protocol unchanged - the device stays the Noise responder; it only sends its server hello
first so the peer can pick the key by name and MAC.

Deep-sleep aware - deep-sleep builds skip the connect delay and dial as soon as the network
is up.

The cost on an ESP32 is 32 B of RAM with outgoing_connection plus a host, 48 B when learning
the target. aioesphomeapi 46.4.0 and Home Assistant core already know how to answer.

Setup wizard for Home Assistant onboarding
Section titled “Setup wizard for Home Assistant onboarding”

@jesserockz added a device-side setup wizard that Home Assistant
can show during onboarding ( #19966 ). A wizard:
block under api: describes a series of pages with device entities to highlight (an enable
switch, for example) and inputs that pick Home Assistant entities the device needs. Inputs can be
linked to a homeassistant -platform entity so the device subscribes to it automatically, or stand
alone as a plain entity id a lambda can use.

The wizard is fixed at build time and compressed with zstd on the Python side, so the device
ships one blob out of flash and the format can grow without new proto fields. On an ESP32-IDF
build a single-switch wizard adds about 0.4 KB of flash; a config with no wizard adds nothing.

NOTE

The wizard will not be shown until Home Assistant 2026.11. Older versions ignore it and add the device as usual.

Light transition state publishing and color names
Section titled “Light transition state publishing and color names”

@nohat added an opt-in transition_state_publish_interval on every
light so Home Assistant and MQTT subscribers see the live value during a fade or flash instead of
just the start and end ( #11968 ). Values below 150
ms are rejected; 200 to 250 ms is a good value. The build pays nothing unless at least one light
sets the option, and each light grows by 8 bytes of RAM when the option is enabled. This also lays
the groundwork for hold-to-dim.

Two other light-side quality-of-life improvements landed from
@clydebarrow: CSS color names and 0xRRGGBB values anywhere a
light state is specified, including strobe and addressable_color_wipe
( #19712,
#19874 ); and resume_effect: from
@TheRealChriAnd that resumes the running effect after a plain
turn-off / turn-on ( #17791 ). restore_mode is
replaced by a more expressive restore_state that can leave, invert or force a specific value per
property, with a warning when a legacy restore_mode would silently discard an explicit
initial_state ( #18997 ).

Host platform builds natively
Section titled “Host platform builds natively”

@jesserockz moved the host platform off PlatformIO onto ninja and
the machine’s own compiler, matching how ESP32 and ESP8266 already build
( #19214 ). Compilers are picked from PATH
( g++ / gcc first, then clang, honouring CC / CXX ), ccache is used when present, and libraries
go through the shared converter into archives. Build-flag routing follows SCons semantics, and
cg.set_cpp_standard replaces the old -std=gnu++20 build flag so C sources never see a C++
standard. Measured on an M5 Max against the same host config and the same 128 objects, a cold
build takes 2.4 s instead of 3.9 s, a no-op rebuild 0.3 s instead of 1.2 to 1.4 s, and a clean
build with a warm ccache 0.5 s instead of 4.0 s.

USB bridging, mux and serial proxy taps
Section titled “USB bridging, mux and serial proxy taps”

A connected effort landed around sharing physical ports between a USB host, an on-device component
and remote API consumers. Starting from @kbx81 ’s new
bridge component with its first cdc_acm_uart platform
( #11689 ), the ESP32-S2/S3/P4 can present as a
USB-to-UART bridge with dynamic line coding, DTR/RTS output, and clean pause() / resume() for
sharing the UART with on-device code. The new uart_mux component
( #19066 ) routes a UART to either the bridge or a
local consumer like zwave_proxy, driven by tinyusb on_mount / on_unmount automations added
in #19067.

Alongside it, serial_proxy grew a protocol-agnostic tap seam and port mode so Home Assistant can
flash through a port that normally carries a protocol
( #18955 ) and a USB_SERIAL port type plus a
SerialProxyIdentity message so clients can target a specific USB device even when the topology
changes ( #19308, by
@puddly ). usb_uart gained descriptor filters for iManufacturer and
iProduct for devices that share VID/PID ( #19095 )
and a claim_comm_interface: false option that frees a USB host hardware channel per device on
channel-poor hosts like the ESP32-S3
( #18969 ).

Networking, ethernet and connectivity
Section titled “Networking, ethernet and connectivity”

TCP-UART bridges - @Bascht74 added two complementary
components: tcp_uart presents a remote TCP socket as a UART, so Modbus
and similar can talk to a network-reachable serial device without an on-device hardware UART
( #19884 ); uart_tcp
copies a hardware UART to a TCP socket in either direction
( #19887 ). A server role with IPv4 allow-lists,
a shared TcpListener, and a diagnostic disconnects counter follow in
#20026,
#20037 and
#20096.

KSZ8851SNL SPI Ethernet - @jesserockz added Microchip’s
KSZ8851SNL to the ethernet component’s SPI chip list, so boards built around it can now use
their Ethernet port ( #19883 ).

Forced WiFi roam check - a new wifi.roam action and force_roam() API call trigger an
immediate roaming scan from automations
( #17349, by
@clydebarrow ).

ESP32 UART clock source - @ikruglov added a clock_source
option that keeps a UART stable through dynamic frequency scaling: a 9600 bps Modbus RTU bus
that was flooded by timeouts under DFS runs cleanly with clock_source: XTAL, and idle power
drops noticeably because DFS becomes usable
( #16486 ).

Signed OTA mDNS and plaintext migration lane
Section titled “Signed OTA mDNS and plaintext migration lane”

@kbx81 made devices built with signed_ota_verification advertise an
ota_signed=1 TXT record on _esphomelib._tcp, so a discovery client like Device Builder knows up
front it needs a trusted key before compiling anything
( #19407 ). To bridge the long tail of devices that
cannot encrypt yet, @bdraco added allow_plaintext_upload: true under
ota: encryption: so one migration install can still land after the plaintext fallback is removed
in 2027.3.0; the uploader logs that the install went plaintext and tells the user to remove the
option once the device is seen encrypting ( #19396 ).

ESPHome Device Builder
Section titled “ESPHome Device Builder”

The bundled ESPHome Device Builder can now flash every
chip family that ESPHome supports from the browser. Before this release, browser flashing worked
only for ESP32 and ESP8266. This section covers the main changes merged since the 2026.9.0 release
notes.

nRF52 - @tomaszduda23 added flashing through the Adafruit
bootloader’s Nordic Legacy DFU (Device Firmware Update) protocol
( frontend#1784 ), MCUboot updates
over Bluetooth and serial
( frontend#1891 ), and logs over USB
serial and Bluetooth
( frontend#1788 ). The Bluetooth
logs reconnect when the link drops
( frontend#1868 ).

Raspberry Pi Pico - RP2040 and RP2350 boards flash over WebUSB with PICOBOOT, the Pico’s USB
boot protocol ( frontend#1785,
frontend#1927 ). Logs work over Web
Serial ( frontend#1786 ). Firefox
has no WebUSB, so it downloads the UF2 firmware file and shows how to copy it to the board.

LibreTiny - Realtek RTL8720C and RTL8710B, Beken BK72xx and Lightning LN882H boards flash over
Web Serial through a USB serial adapter
( frontend#1796,
frontend#1977,
frontend#1929,
frontend#1972 ). Logs work over Web
Serial too ( frontend#1804,
frontend#1934,
frontend#1973 ).

Plain HTTP dashboards - browsers block USB access when the dashboard is served over plain
HTTP. In that case the dashboard sends the firmware to ESPHome Web, which flashes it. This already
worked for ESP; it now works for every family above
( frontend#1869,
frontend#1923,
frontend#1926,
frontend#1935,
frontend#1978 ).

ESPHome Web - web.esphome.io supports the same families. nRF52 gets
logs and MCUboot updates
( frontend#1799,
frontend#1913 ). Pico boards flash
over PICOBOOT ( frontend#1814 ).
BK72xx and LN882H are new
( frontend#1933,
frontend#1973 ). RTL8720C and
RTL8710B share one RTL87xx entry that reads the chip from the firmware file
( frontend#1986 ).

Other Device Builder changes in this release:

Signed OTA devices - a device that advertises ota_signed=1 rejects any OTA update that is
not signed by a key it trusts. After adoption, the user’s own build is unsigned. When the config
has no signing key, @kbx81 made the dashboard flash the first build
over USB
( #2895,
frontend#1991 ).

Faster OTA builds - OTA updates compile with the new --skip-bootloader flag. On ESP32, the
build skips the bootloader and factory image, which an OTA update never uses. This saves tens of
seconds per device on a Home Assistant Green. Other platforms run a full build as before
( #2874 ).

Optional MCP endpoint - MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a standard way for an AI assistant to
call tools. The new /api/mcp endpoint lets an MCP client, such as Home Assistant’s MCP
integration, read and edit configs, add components and automations, and validate, compile and
install ( #2733,
#2736,
#2789 ). It is optional. The Device Builder
never calls an AI model itself. The endpoint does nothing until you connect an MCP client, and
everything else works the same without one.

Offline duration - @siegeld added how long a device has been
offline. The status pill shows Offline 2h
( #2842,
frontend#1862 ).

Network column - @davidcoulson added a Network column and
filter. It shows whether a device uses WiFi or Ethernet
( #2692,
frontend#1737 ).

Analyze memory - Expert Mode has a new action that runs esphome analyze-memory. It shows the
flash and RAM use of each component ( #2835,
frontend#1816 ).

Flash chip setting - the ESP32 framework form shows the new flash_chip option
( #2870 ).

Version history - the Device Builder now only commits to a git repository rooted at the
ESPHome config directory. If your whole Home Assistant /config is a git repository, ESPHome
edits are no longer committed to it
( #2882 ).

New components
Section titled “New components”

The release adds a strong batch of new components and platforms:

tfluna by @candrews adds the
Benewake TF-Luna I2C LiDAR with distance, signal strength and temperature sensors
( #9199 ).

bridge + cdc_acm_uart by
@kbx81 - the USB-UART bridge dom…

articles.title: ESPHome 2026.10 brings faster builds and smaller updates
articles.dek: The October release also broadens browser flashing, with settings to check before upgrading.
body: ESPHome 2026.10 arrives today with less waiting when building and updating homemade devices. Its native ESP8266 build tools become the default, removing the need for Rosetta on Apple Silicon Macs. The first build after upgrading starts clean; the older PlatformIO path remains an opt-out until its planned removal in April 2027.

Wireless firmware updates add compression on ESP32, RP2040, LibreTiny and host systems. The official release notes report roughly a third fewer bytes to transfer, helping slow connections; compatible firmware and upload tools negotiate compression automatically. Older firmware continues to update through the existing path.

The bundled Device Builder also extends browser flashing beyond ESP32 and ESP8266 to Nordic, Raspberry Pi Pico and LibreTiny chips. Browser support still matters: Firefox users installing Pico firmware receive a file and instructions to copy it to the board.

Before updating, check lights with a configured initial state: a light set to start on now follows that setting instead of silently staying off. Speaker media players must remove the obsolete codec_support_enabled option; format: NONE preserves its former all-codecs setting. The release notes list the remaining configuration and upgrade changes.

externalSources.title: ESPHome 2026.10.0: Native ESP8266 builds and compressed updates

articles.title: Home Assistant installs patch updates in a chosen time window
articles.dek: An optional automatic updater respects skipped versions, backups and the running release series.
body: Home Assistant OS gains automatic installation of patch updates within the owner’s chosen time window. The optional updater chooses an eligible patch for the running release series after the configured waiting period, leaving skipped versions alone.

It avoids safe mode and waits while a Core update or backup is already running. Each installation uses a saved, randomly chosen point within the window and makes one attempt per window. Installation follows the existing update process, including a backup when enabled and Supervisor’s health checks and rollback handling.
The version must still be offered by Supervisor, so withdrawing a release prevents it from being selected.

pullRequests.title: Install Home Assistant patch releases automatically on schedule

articles.title: Matter.js keeps device pairings through controller upgrades
articles.dek: Version 0.18 also supports Matter 1.6.1 and checks whether device implementations meet the specification.
body: Makers of Matter controllers can move to Matter.js’s completed new controller interface without pairing every device again. Version 0.18 keeps the same stored pairing format for both interfaces, with a migration guide for developers; the old interface and its package are planned for removal in version 0.19.

The release also adds the device types and protocol features from Matter 1.6.1 for people building devices, bridges and controllers. It checks each endpoint against its device definition, warning about missing requirements by default and offering stricter checks during development.

Upgrading device and bridge implementations may require explicitly selecting features that were previously chosen automatically. The announcement asks developers to review the new validation warnings. This release supplies tools for software built with Matter.js; connected smart-home platforms still need their own implementation of its capabilities.

articles.title: ESPHome gives doorbells and spoken alerts their own volume
articles.dek: An optional setting keeps idle announcements from inheriting the last music level.
body: An ESPHome speaker’s next doorbell, timer or spoken announcement need not be almost silent because music was turned down the night before—or startlingly loud because it was left high. An optional announcement volume applies when an announcement begins while normal media is idle, paused or off.

Announcements over playing music keep the music volume. After the announcement queue and buffered audio finish, the normal level returns; starting music restores it immediately. Mute still keeps the speaker silent, and the setting does not overwrite the saved media volume.

pullRequests.title: [speaker][speaker_source] Add a set volume for announcements that start while nothing is playing
[speaker] Document announcement volume

articles.title: Music Assistant searches music collections through AudioMuse-AI
articles.dek: A connected analysis server finds similar tracks and offers optional text searches across Jellyfin, Navidrome and Plex.
body: Music Assistant connects to AudioMuse-AI to find music by its sound and, optionally, by a free-text request. The open-source analysis server supplies similar tracks for radio mode and an “Inspired by recently played” row; its optional search uses audio analysis and lyrics.

Setup connects to a running AudioMuse-AI server and maps its results to the matching music source. Jellyfin and Navidrome support is joined by a correction for Plex’s different track identifiers. Similarity plugins also take priority over suggestions from the track’s music service, so installing one actually changes which recommendations are chosen.
NeptuneHub makes a first contribution to Music Assistant’s server with the new connection, with Marvin Schenkel completing the Plex support and recommendation ordering.

pullRequests.title: AudioMuse-AI provider
Support Plex in the AudioMuse-AI provider
Similar tracks from a similarity plugin take precedence over the music provider

articles.title: Home Assistant places pharmacy orders through Mijn Farmad Apotheek
articles.dek: A new connection searches prices and stock, with payment at collection.
body: Home Assistant adds medication search and ordering through Mijn Farmad Apotheek, a service used by more than a thousand pharmacies in Flanders. An automation can look up a product’s price and stock, then place an order for collection at a chosen connected pharmacy.

Search accepts a product name or its Belgian catalog code and returns up to 25 results. Ordering takes one product code, with payment handled at pickup. Accounts requiring multi-factor authentication are outside this first connection’s scope. DaanVervacke describes the motivation as making repeat orders easier to remember.

pullRequests.title: Add Mijn Farmad Apotheek integration
Add Mijn Farmad Apotheek documentation

articles.title: Home Assistant finds the right overnight transit departure
articles.dek: GTFS timetables keep their service dates and agency timezone, with a change needed for manual timezone offsets.
body: Home Assistant corrects transit departure readings around midnight and across timezones. Night routes whose services all run after midnight stop incorrectly reporting that no departures remain, while tomorrow’s first journey receives tomorrow’s date instead of a timestamp in the past.
The GTFS connection also selects the next departure using the transit agency’s timezone. Comparing against Home Assistant’s own timezone could otherwise choose a bus or train that had already left.

Owners who used the offset setting specifically to compensate for a timezone difference need to remove that workaround when adopting the correction; keeping it applies the adjustment twice. Other uses of the offset are separate from that timezone workaround.

pullRequests.title: Fix GTFS next departure when the feed time zone differs
Fix GTFS missing past-midnight departures before midnight
Fix GTFS include_tomorrow departures using today's date

articles.title: Home Assistant keeps energy costs through restarts and unit changes
articles.dek: Usage while the system is stopped gains a cost, and changing a meter’s display unit stops creating false charges.
body: Home Assistant preserves the last meter reading it priced when it shuts down, allowing the next start to account for consumption during the interruption. Previously, the first reading after a restart became a fresh baseline without a cost; for a meter read once a day, that could omit an entire day’s usage.

A related correction handles changes in meter units. Switching from kilowatt-hours to watt-hours no longer subtracts values in different units and charges roughly the whole meter reading again. Energy, gas and water cost calculations convert the earlier reading when possible; an incompatible change starts pricing from the new reading.

pullRequests.title: Price energy used while Home Assistant was stopped
Handle meter unit changes in energy cost sensor

articles.title: Music Assistant stops newer Cast speakers cutting streams short
articles.dek: A default connection change avoids an observed limit that stopped radio and skipped tracks after a few minutes.
body: Music Assistant changes its streaming default for newer Android-based Cast receivers, including the 2026 Google Home Speaker and Android TV sticks. These receivers stopped a stream after about 24 MiB when sent a stated content length—roughly ten minutes of high-quality MP3 or three to four minutes of FLAC—then advanced the queue or stopped radio.

The connection no longer sends that length by default. Existing custom choices are preserved, while players still using the default follow the correction automatically. Separate decoding failures remain outside this fix; with flow mode disabled, individual tracks also lose the duration display on the receiver.

pullRequests.title: Fix newer Google Cast speakers stopping after about 24 MiB

articles.title: Home Assistant keeps UniFi connected after the Network 11 upgrade
articles.dek: A changed site identifier stops requiring owners to delete and recreate their integration.
body: Home Assistant reconnects to existing UniFi sites after Network 11 changes their identifiers. Previously, the integration could fail to load until the owner recreated it or edited its stored configuration by hand.

The correction recognizes that specific identifier change and finds the same site by its configured name on the same controller. It preserves the integration’s entity names, areas, disabled settings and device identities.

Wi-Fi networks and traffic rules also receive new identifiers from UniFi and are outside this repair, so their entities are still recreated. Other kinds of site-identifier change are deliberately left alone.

pullRequests.title: Follow UniFi site ID change in Network 11

articles.title: Music Assistant moves Apple Music stations into Radio
articles.dek: Saved favourites and history follow the move, but automations using old station links need attention.
body: Apple Music stations appear under Radio in Music Assistant instead of being treated as dynamic playlists. Radio searches and shared station links resolve to the same kind of item, making stations easier to find alongside other radio sources.

Saved stations move with their favourites, artwork and listening history. Existing Home Assistant automations and smart-playlist seeds that use the old playlist address need the station selected again to obtain its radio address. Saving a station remains local to Music Assistant; it does not add it to an Apple account’s library.

pullRequests.title: Show Apple Music stations under Radio

articles.title: Home Assistant filters media folders that cannot search
articles.dek: A local filter narrows long channel lists and other loaded folders without requiring support from the source.
body: Home Assistant adds a filter to media-browser folders containing ten or more items when their source does not support search. A long television channel list can be narrowed by name instead of scrolling through every channel.

The filter checks the items already loaded and ignores capitalization and accents, so typing “stefan” also finds “Ștefan”. Sources with their own search keep it, and moving to another folder clears the filter.

pullRequests.title: Filter long media browser folders locally when the source cannot search

media.caption: A mock channel list demonstrates the filter matching a name without its accent.

articles.title: Home Assistant handles the repeated hour when clocks go back
articles.dek: Schedule helpers stop repeatedly firing a past timer, while time triggers and statistics keep the correct period.
body: Home Assistant fixes a schedule-helper failure during the repeated hour when daylight saving time ends. A timer could select the first occurrence of a time that had already passed and immediately reschedule itself thousands of times per second; it now chooses the upcoming occurrence.

Related time handling preserves automation matches when a timezone moves back by half an hour or changes off the hour, including Lord Howe and Chatham. Statistics also retain a final day, week or month containing a clock change when the available readings end in that period’s first hour.

articles.title: ESPHome reaches MQTT brokers through web-only connections
articles.dek: ESP32 devices using ESP-IDF can carry their messaging over WebSocket connections, including encrypted HTTPS.
body: ESPHome adds a way for ESP32 devices using ESP-IDF to reach an MQTT broker behind a proxy or tunnel that only passes web traffic. MQTT carries sensor readings and commands; the new transport sends those messages over WebSocket connections, including an encrypted option for HTTPS routes.

Encrypted connections check the broker against the firmware’s certificate bundle when no custom authority is configured. Ordinary TCP stays the default, and other chip platforms and ESP32 Arduino builds are outside this addition’s scope.

pullRequests.title: [mqtt] Add MQTT over WebSocket transport for ESP32 IDF
Document MQTT over WebSocket transport for ESP32 IDF

articles.title: Custom Home Assistant sign-ins need an explicit second-factor check
articles.dek: A November compatibility change requires action from authors of unsupported custom authentication providers.
body: Home Assistant’s contributor guidance warns that custom integrations which supply their own authentication provider must update their login flow for Core 2026.11. Without the change, those providers stop requesting a second factor, even when they previously relied on Home Assistant to add that step.

Josef Zweck explains how to use the new MFA-aware login flow and finish authentication through its checking method. This warning applies to custom authentication providers, which Home Assistant does not support; it is not an instruction for ordinary household accounts to disable or reconfigure their two-factor settings.

externalSources.title: Auth providers now opt in to multi-factor authentication

articles.title: Assist recognizes Turkish device names more reliably
articles.dek: Dotted and dotless letters stop hiding matching devices and number words from recognition.
body: Hassil, the sentence parser behind Assist, stops discarding Turkish device names because their capital and lowercase forms use different versions of the letter i. A request to turn off “Salon Işığı” can match the lowercased words returned by speech recognition instead of appearing to name an unknown light.

A companion correction recognizes number words with the same letter variations and keeps their positions correct when an earlier word contains a dotted capital İ. Akın Ömeroğlu makes a first contribution to Hassil with the device-name correction; Michael Hansen extends the handling to number words.

pullRequests.title: Fold the Turkish dotless i in the candidate index
Match number words written with any Turkish I

articles.title: Home Assistant’s Windows installer blocks a substituted PowerShell
articles.dek: The administrator-level installer starts PowerShell from the Windows system directory.
body: Home Assistant’s Windows installer stops looking up PowerShell by its program name. That lookup could run a different powershell.exe placed beside the installer, such as in Downloads, with the installer’s administrator privileges.
It instead uses the full path returned by Windows for its system directory. This closes that command-selection route without relying on the contents of the installer’s folder.

pullRequests.title: Start PowerShell from the system directory

articles.title: Music Assistant enforces Tidal’s one-stream account limit
articles.dek: A second independent stream waits or reports the limit instead of starting alongside the first.
body: Music Assistant limits each Tidal account to one simultaneous source stream. A second room trying to open another stream must wait for the slot or receives a stream-limit error.
Setup also refuses to connect the same account through another Tidal instance. Existing duplicate connections keep working, but reconnecting one is refused until the other is removed.

pullRequests.title: Limit Tidal to one concurrent stream per account

articles.title: Home Assistant restores durations and Marketplace on older browsers
articles.dek: Duration and relative-time displays recover on Safari and iOS 12–13 and Chrome 59–66.
body: Home Assistant repairs duration, relative-time and Marketplace formatting on Safari and iOS 12–13 and Chrome 59–66. Those browsers could not load the newer number-formatting code, leaving some views broken. A fallback restores the formatting while preserving the browsers’ native date handling.

pullRequests.title: Restore FormatJS Intl polyfills on browsers without BigInt

roadmapUpdates.title: Work begins on exclusions for automation targets
roadmapUpdates.summary: Niels’s proposal to exclude individual entities from an area, floor or label target moves from Approved to Building. It aims to preserve those exclusions as the target changes, letting an automation follow a whole room while leaving selected devices alone.

sources.title: Let users exclude individual entities from resolved targets in automations/blueprints/scripts

roadmapUpdates.title: Replacing automation steps receives approval
roadmapUpdates.summary: Franck Nijhof approves Niels’s proposal to replace a trigger, condition or action without rebuilding the row, assigning it low priority. This advances the revised plan reported yesterday from Awaiting approval to Approved.

sources.title: Let people change their mind about an automation step without rebuilding it
